newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Afghanistan says Taleban deported 60,000 to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan says Taleban deported 60,000 to Kabul.

text.p: Afghanistan has accused the Islamic Taleban movement of deporting more than 60,000 people to Kabul from a recently-captured region north of the capital and called on the United Nations to enable them to return home.

The appeal was made in identical letters to the U.N. secretary-general and the president of the Security Council from Abdul Rahim Ghafoorzai, acting foreign minister in the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, ousted when Taleban captured Kabul last September but still recognised by the United Nations.
He said Taleban forces on Jan. 16 attacked and occupied part of Charikar, the capital of Parwan province north of Kabul.

"With the motive of tearing apart the whole national fabric of Afghan society in general, and of terrorising the civilian population of the province in particular, the Taleban mercenaries on January 17 forcible transferred and deported more than 60,000 members of the population of Charikar and other townships of the province to the capital, Kabul."
He said the forcible exodus was mostly of the elderly, women and children, and took place during the Moslem holy month of fasting, Ramadan.

Ghafoorzai said most of the people left behind all their possessions and, because of a lack of transport, were forced to walk a long distance to Kabul, itself a war-ravaged city lacking even basic public services.

"The heinous policy of coercive eviction and mass deportation of the civilian population, which is a crime against humanity, is being carried out in Afghanistan while elsewhere in the world the perpetrators of such crimes are subject to special jurisdiction, established to prosecute and punish them," he added, alluding to U.N. war crimes tribunals for the former Yugoslavia and Rwanda.
Ghafoozai said Afghanistan called on the secretary-general, the Security Council and other U.N. agencies and intergovernmental bodies to "pay immediate and urgent attention to the matter."

"The United Nations is called upon to immediately intervene to prepare the circumstances allowing all civilians who have been deported and forcibly displaced to return to their homes without being subjected to discrimination on the basis of gender, age or ethnic origin."
